analysis.title: GS Kamshad - GS TMT TODAY 11.2.26
key_insights: Futures are bid to start the week (Nasdaq +60bps, S&P +30bps, Russell +45bps) after Friday's tech/AI-driven sell-off. WTI is down about 4% on reports that Trump wants to give Iran diplomacy more time and that Iranian negotiators left Doha with a draft proposal circulating.
GS Risk Appetite Indicator recorded October's largest drop in global risk appetite since November 2021, and a top-5 drop in the last 15 years.

Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in a $115B all-stock deal. Lumentum holders get 4.500 Marvell shares per share (about $1,132 per share, a 23.9% premium to Oct 28 unaffected closes). Marvell holders will own about 67% of the combined company. Close is expected in 1H 2028, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

SpaceX is in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile or use its network (Washington Post). Verizon, T-Mobile and AT&T had refused SpaceX network access, and Boost leases its network from AT&T and T-Mobile. ECHO was +7% and TMUS/T/VZ -2% premarket.
Oracle is set to start a 6-part, $10bn bond offering (Bloomberg). Okta joins the S&P 500 effective November 4. CRWD is +3% on a Deutsche Bank upgrade.

GS Research added Amphenol (APH) to the US Conviction List (23 names). Mark Delaney expects topline growth faster than expected from its data center, industrial, aerospace and military mix plus M&A. His 2027 EBITDA estimate is 10% above Street consensus.

Callahan (GS specialist sales): the NDX fell about 7% in October, its second worst month since the AI cycle began in early 2023, and is in its third 10%+ correction of the year. Demand drivers (token demand, GW/DC build-outs) are intact, but the market is questioning the linearity of the AI build-out beyond CY27, pressuring multiples.

Callahan: the Mon-Wed bounce faded despite a benign FOMC and robust 3Q earnings. Investors are looking to broaden out, but there is no bearish tilt on AI suppliers. Non-AI names are hard to find that avoid AI-disruption narratives, and AAPL, SNPS, ADI/TXN/NXPI, SPOT, V/MA, EBAY and LYV held up well.

Macro: E-minis +50bps, Nasdaq futures +75bps, US 10-year yield lower at 4.91%, crude -4.5%. The week is catalyst-heavy: 21% of SPX market cap reports, midterm elections, Treasury Quarterly Refunding Announcement and payrolls.

Asia finished mixed (Shanghai +1.08%, Hang Seng +42bps, Nikkei -33bps, Kospi +2.24%). The PBOC reportedly met financial firms and introduced market stabilization measures. China manufacturing and non-manufacturing PMIs fell into contraction. Tokyo Electron +5% on results, Kioxia -15% after a 3Q forecast miss. Europe was up slightly on volumes 25% below the 10-day average.

Prime Services: hedge funds were net buyers of US equities for the first time in 4 weeks, driven by short covers in macro products and some single stocks. Info Tech was the most net bought sector through Thursday but is still heavily net sold month-to-date in October. Mag 7 were net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions.

Prime: Friday's sell-off was aggressive with little defense, and ETFs were about 31% of the tape, the highest full-session share since June. Supply was concentrated in tech but orderly versus the prior two weeks. S&P levels watched: 100-day average at 7614 and CTA medium-term threshold at 7554.

Russell 2000 outperformed the NDX and SPX on the week. CFTC data through Oct 20 show net positioning rebounded on new length, with sizable shorts remaining. GS systematic momentum thresholds would flip negative if Friday's price action persists, halting projected CTA buying.

Derivatives: NDX 1-month fixed strike vol fell almost 4 vol points early in the week, then rose almost 2 on Friday. Gamma has not repriced as much as vol and skew. The straddle through Wednesday's close, covering the midterms, priced 1.51% versus Friday's S&P move of -1.82%.

Midterm affordability baskets: long ACA-exposed beneficiaries (GSHLCACA), short drug-makers (GSHLCBPH), long renewables/grid/power (GSXURNEW, GSXUGRID, GSENEPOW), buy protection on hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) and datacenter equipment (GSTMTDAT), and long government-spending exposed ex-defense and drug-makers (GSXUGOVT) versus short defense spending beneficiaries (GSXUDFNS).

Semis closed down about 8% on Friday, the 3rd largest day of underperformance in over 15 years. Drivers cited were a mixed Kioxia guide, a big INTC guide down, uneven 2H hyperscaler capex and an AMKR smartphone downtick.

GS raised its global data center supply forecast to 273GW by 2030 from 217GW in July 2026, adding 170GW after 2025, with net additions of 25GW/32GW/35GW in 2026/27/28. At $50B/GW this implies $8.5tn of capex over 5 years.

TrendForce expects 4Q26 DRAM ASP for PC/server/mobile of +13-18%/+10-15%/+0-5% qoq, and eMMC/UFS +4-9%. This is above GS estimates for PC DRAM, in line for server and mobile DRAM, and below GS for NAND. GS reiterates Buy on SEC (on Conviction List) and Hynix.

South Korea October exports: DRAM exports at a record US$34bn (+595% yoy), memory +359% yoy for a 9th straight month above +200%, display +29%, Li-ion batteries +21%, MLCC +37%, WFE equipment +197%. October had 22 working days versus 20 a year earlier.

Kioxia CY3Q26 read-across: results solid, NAND supply/demand expected to stay tight through CY27, and multi-year long-term agreements give demand visibility beyond CY27-28. GS keeps Buy on SEC and Hynix.

Street actions: upgrades of AMZN (Buy, Phillip Securities), COHR (Outperform, Northland), CRWD (Buy, Deutsche Bank) and RIVN (Buy, UBS). RDDT downgraded to Hold by Loop Capital. FIG initiated at Neutral by Rothschild.

Calendar: Mon ISM Manufacturing and Construction Spending, Goolsbee 11:15am, AAPL/PLTR/ON/VRTX post-close. Tue JOLTS and midterms, with AMD/ANET/BKNG/SHOP earnings. Wed Services PMI, EU flash inflation, QCOM/ARM/UBER/DDOG/APP earnings. Thu BoE decision, NET/ABNB/AXON/LYV earnings. Fri payrolls (prior +29k).

tension_points.bull_case: The directional engine of the market (token demand plus GW/DC build-outs) remains intact. GS raised its 2030 data center supply forecast to 273GW, and memory pricing and exports are at records. Multi-year LTAs give NAND demand visibility beyond CY27-28.
tension_points.bear_case: The market is questioning the linearity of the AI build-out beyond CY27, pressuring multiples. Semis fell about 8% Friday on a weak INTC guide, uneven 2H hyperscaler capex and an AMKR smartphone downtick, and Mag 7 flows show little recovery in risk appetite.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If Friday's price action persists, GS systematic momentum thresholds flip negative and projected CTA buying stops. S&P levels watched are the 100-day average at 7614 and the CTA threshold at 7554.
